'''Rodrigue Gabriel "Roddy" Beaubois'''<ref>{{Cite web |title=Rodrigue Beaubois |url=https://www.acb.com/jugador/temporada-a-temporada/id/20212200 |access-date=17 June 2022 |website=ACB.com |language=es}}</ref> ({{IPA|fr|ʁɑdʁiɡ bobwɑ}}; born 24 February 1988) is a French professional [[basketball]] player who last played for [[Anadolu Efes S.K.|Anadolu Efes]] of the Turkish [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL) and the [[EuroLeague]].

== Early life ==
Beaubois was discovered by [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] player [[Mickaël Piétrus]] at an open basketball camp in his native home island, [[Guadeloupe]], located in the [[French West Indies]].<ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/rodrigue_beaubois/bio.html | title= Rodrigue Beaubois | website= [[NBA.com]] | date=22 February 2008}}</ref> He made his professional debut in the 2006–07 season with [[Cholet Basket]] in the [[Ligue Nationale de Basketball|French Pro A League]], where he was teammates with future [[Toronto Raptors]] guard [[Nando de Colo]].<ref>[http://www.draftexpress.com/article/Nando-De-Colo-I-want-to-play-in-the-NBA-3230/ Nando De Colo: "I want to play in the NBA"]</ref>

== Professional career ==

=== Cholet Basket (2006–2009) ===

In his first season with Cholet Basket, Beaubois played with the Cholet Espoirs, the junior team, where he averaged 10.8 points, 2.1 rebounds, 2.3 assists and 18.1 minutes per game. Beaubois spent the majority of the [[2006–07 LNB Pro A season|2006–07 season]] with the Espoirs, averaging 13.2 points, 4.0 rebounds and 3.4 assists. He saw action in four French Pro A League games, in which he never scored. He also played 3 minutes in the 2007 Pro A playoffs, losing in the quarterfinals to [[Chorale Roanne Basket|Roanne]].<ref>[http://www.lnb.fr/fr/Pro-A/200010/Stats-Joueurs/A35923/fiche?type=1&from=2006&stat=m Beaubois 2006/07 statistics]</ref>

Beaubois missed the first few weeks of the [[2007–08 LNB Pro A season|2007–08 season]] due to a fractured bone in his left hand. He would play in the French Pro A League the whole season, averaging 5.5 points, 1.8 rebounds, and 1.4 assists in 15.1 minutes per game. He scored in double figures five times, recording a season high of 15 points against [[ASVEL Basket]].<ref>[http://www.lnb.fr/fr/Pro-A/200009/Resultat-match/2754/resultat-match Match Results Cholet – Lyon-Villeurbanne]</ref> Beaubois would lose in the quarterfinals again this time to [[Le Mans Sarthe Basket|Le Mans]].<ref>[http://www.lnb.fr/fr/Pro-A/200009/Resultat-match/3355/resultat-match RÉSULTATS DU MATCH CHOLET – LE MANS]</ref> Cholet Basket competed in the [[2007–08 FIBA EuroCup|2007–08 FIBA EuroChallenge.]] The [[FIBA EuroChallenge|EuroChallenge]] is the third tier in the [[2007–08 FIBA EuroCup|European professional club basketball pyramid]]. Beaubois played in 3 games and averaged 4.7 points and 1 rebound and assists in 18.7 minutes.<ref>[http://www.fibaeurope.com/cid_KNce8jInH7Qj1EsyH5rjn2.compID_BYg5Rb55Jw-G5I3MZ6JB01.roundID_5839.season_2008.teamID_1171.playerID_61807.html Beaubois 2007-08 FIBA EuroCup stats]</ref> Cholet lost in the [[EuroCup 2007–08 Group D|group stage]] of the competition going 2–4.

In his 29 games of the [[2008–09 LNB Pro A season|2008–09 season]], Beaubois averaged 10 points, 2.5 rebounds, 2.3 assists and 1.1 steals per game in 22.3 minutes. He improved as the season progressed. Notably, he recorded a career high 31 points, eight assists and five steals against Roanne.<ref>[http://www.lnb.fr/fr/Pro-A/200009/Resultat-match/3626/resultat-match Match Results Cholet – Roanne]</ref> Cholet Basket did not qualify for the 2009 playoffs, but they participated in the second tier of the European professional club basketball pyramid. After losing to [[ASK Riga]] in the [[2008–09 Eurocup Basketball|Eurocup]] preliminary rounds,<ref>[http://www.fibaeurope.com/cid_KNce8jInH7Qj1EsyH5rjn2.gameID_6520-8-B-2.compID_BYg5Rb55Jw-G5I3MZ6JB01.season_2009.roundID_6491.teamID_.html Cholet Basket – ASK Riga]</ref> Cholet competed again in the EuroChallenge. During the [[2008–09 FIBA EuroChallenge|2008–09 EuroChallenge]], Beaubois nearly had a triple double, scoring 16 points, grabbing nine rebounds, and assisting eight times against [[Fribourg Olympic]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.angers.maville.com/actu/actudet_-Basket-ball.-EuroChallenge-Cholet-Fribourg-79-52-_39916-777273_actu.Htm |title=Basket-ball. EuroChallenge : Cholet – Fribourg (79-52) |access-date=13 July 2013 |archive-date=14 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211114073846/https://angers.maville.com/actu/actudet_-Basket-ball.-EuroChallenge-Cholet-Fribourg-79-52-_39916-777273_actu.Htm |url-status=dead }}</ref> Cholet would advance to the EuroChallenge Final Four, only to lose to [[Virtus Bologna]].<ref>[http://www.fibaeurope.com/cid_KNce8jInH7Qj1EsyH5rjn2.compID_BYg5Rb55Jw-G5I3MZ6JB01.season_2009.coid_4ihJxgKmGQ-HZmQI,0ZyJ2.articleMode_on.html Virtus BolognaFiere Beat Brave Cholet]</ref>

=== Dallas Mavericks (2009–2013) ===
[[File:Rodrigue Beaubois 2.jpg|thumb|right|Beaubois with the [[Dallas Mavericks]] in 2011]]
Beaubois was an early entry candidate for the [[2007 NBA draft|2007]] and [[2008 NBA draft]] before withdrawing his name from consideration. Prior to the [[NBA draft]], Beaubois caught the attention of scouts at the [[NBA Draft Combine]] with his measurements, boasting a 6' 9.75" wingspan (which is extraordinarily long, given his height) and 39" vertical leap.<ref>[http://www.mynbadraft.com/2009-nba-draft-measurements/ 2009 NBA Draft Measurements]</ref> He was selected 25th overall in the [[2009 NBA draft]] by the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]], who traded him, along with a future 2nd round draft pick, to the [[Dallas Mavericks]] for [[Byron Mullens]], the 24th overall pick in the 2009 NBA draft.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/news/transactions/2008_09/ Transactions: 2008-09 Season]</ref>

Playing only 3 minutes, Beaubois made his NBA debut against the [[Los Angeles Lakers]]. On 5 March 2010, Beaubois scored 22 points against the [[Sacramento Kings]], becoming the first Maverick rookie to score 20 or more points since [[Maurice Ager]] in 2007. 22 days later, Beaubois scored a career-high 40 points and made a rookie record of 9 of 11 three-pointers against fellow rookie [[Steph Curry]] and the [[Golden State Warriors]]. Moreover, he became the first rookie in NBA history to shoot at least 50 percent from the floor, 40 percent from 3-point range, and 80 percent from the free throw line. He became the third Maverick rookie with 40 or more points in a game. The Mavericks finished the season with a 55–27 record, clinching the second seed in the Western Conference. In the first round of the [[2010 NBA Playoffs]], Dallas faced their rival the [[San Antonio Spurs]]. The Mavericks were down by 22 points in the first half of Game 6. Needing a spark to the offense, coach [[Rick Carlisle]] subbed Beaubois in and he led them back into the game scoring 16 points, although the Mavericks lost the game and series.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/games/20100429/DALSAS/gameinfo.html#nbaGIboxscore Spurs survive Dallas' rally to close out first round]</ref>

In early August 2010, Beaubois broke his foot while training with the French national basketball team.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/dallas/nba/news/story?id=5443649 Mavs' Rodrigue Beaubois breaks foot]</ref> On 30 November 2010, Beaubois was assigned to the [[Texas Legends]] of the [[NBA G League|NBA D-League]], but never played a single game with the team.<ref>[http://realgm.com/src_wiretap_archives/70326/20101130/mavs_send_beaubois_jones_to_d_league/ Mavs Send Beaubois, Jones To D-League] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101203001426/http://realgm.com/src_wiretap_archives/70326/20101130/mavs_send_beaubois_jones_to_d_league |date=3 December 2010 }}</ref> In February 2011 he returned to practice with the Mavericks.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/dallas/nba/news/story?id=6102177|title=Rodrigue Beaubois back at practice|date=8 February 2011|work=ESPN|access-date=9 February 2011}}</ref> After missing nearly 6 months due to a fractured foot, Beaubois made his season debut against the [[Sacramento Kings]] on 16 February 2011. In 21 minutes, he logged 13 points, 6 assists, 3 steals and 3 turnovers. The Mavericks went on to win the game 116–100. The following game against the [[Phoenix Suns]] Beaubois replaced [[DeShawn Stevenson]] in the starting lineup. Just before the start of the [[2011 NBA Playoffs|2011 playoffs]] Beaubois sprained his left foot in a game against the Warriors. He was replaced in the starting line-up by Stevenson and did not return to action or see playing time during the two-month playoff run leading to the Mavericks' victories over the [[Portland Trail Blazers|Blazers]], Lakers, Thunder, and [[Miami Heat|Heat]] en route to their first NBA Championship.

In late June 2011, Beaubois had foot surgery on his left foot for the second time.<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20130124184052/http://www.google.com/hostednews/afp/article/ALeqM5iukDScPW-xSu40GadTTdDS0Hi3Lw?docId=CNG.3963d77bb5abed477d86934d03b2763e.10e1|title=Beaubois has second surgery}}</ref> The Mavericks announced on 30 June 2011, that they exercised the contract option for Beaubois.<ref>[http://mavsblog.dallasnews.com/archives/2011/06/rodrigue-beaubois-and-dominique-jones-wi.html Dallas exercises Beaubois' option]</ref> In his first start of the [[2011–12 Dallas Mavericks season|2011–12 season]], Beaubois scored 22 points and grabbed 6 rebounds, adding career highs in assists with 7 and blocks with 4, in a win over the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/games/20120127/UTADAL/gameinfo.html Beaubois career night]</ref> Dallas was swept in first round of the [[2012 NBA Playoffs|2012 playoffs]] by Oklahoma City.<ref>{{cite news |title=Mavericks Are Swept Off Their Throne by Thunder (Published 2012) |work=The New York Times |date=6 May 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220621072836/https://www.nytimes.com/2012/05/06/sports/basketball/thunder-sweep-mavericks-with-win-at-dallas.html |archive-date=2022-06-21 |url-status=live |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2012/05/06/sports/basketball/thunder-sweep-mavericks-with-win-at-dallas.html |last1=Spousta |first1=Tom }}</ref>

Beaubois scored a team high (and personal season high) of 19 points in 16 minutes against the Spurs on 25 January 2013.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400278359 Tony Parker returns from cut over eye to lead Spurs]</ref> He underwent surgery to repair a fractured second metacarpal in his left hand near the end of the [[2012-13 Dallas Mavericks season|2012–13 season]]. "I feel bad for the kid," [[Dirk Nowitzki]] said after Beaubois broke his hand against the Thunder on 17 March. "It's just sad. Just so many injuries. He's been here for four years and has missed a lot of action. It's tough. We feel bad for him. But he's a good kid."<ref>[https://www.espn.com/blog/dallas/mavericks/post/_/id/4695035/rodrigue-beaubois-out-indefinitely-with-fractured-hand Beaubois out indefinitely (fractured hand)]</ref><ref name="n956">{{cite web | last=MacMahon | first=Tim | title=Rodrigue Beaubois undergoes hand surgery | website=ESPN.com | date=2013-03-21 | url=https://www.espn.com/blog/dallas/mavericks/post/_/id/4695117/rodrigue-beaubois-undergoes-hand-surgery | access-date=2024-10-15}}</ref> The Mavericks missed the playoffs for the first time since the [[1999–2000 Dallas Mavericks season|1999–00 season]].<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400278889 Mavs eliminated from playoff contention for first time since 2000]</ref>

=== Spirou Charleroi (2014) ===
On 26 March 2014, he signed with [[Spirou Charleroi]] of the [[Basketball League Belgium Division I|Belgian League]] for the rest of the 2013–14 season.<ref>[http://belgacomspirou.sudinfo.be/news/rodrigue-beaubois-terminera-la-saison-a-charleroi Rodrigue Beaubois terminera la saison à Charleroi !] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140328011720/http://belgacomspirou.sudinfo.be/news/rodrigue-beaubois-terminera-la-saison-a-charleroi |date=28 March 2014 }}</ref> Beaubois averaged 9.4 points, 3.8 rebounds and 2.4 assists in 25.4 minutes per game for Spirou.<ref>{{Cite news | url = http://ethiasleague.com/nl/statistieken/spelers/?id=A35923 | title = Rodrigue BEAUBOIS (Belgacom Spirou) | work = Ethias League | access-date= 19 June 2014}}</ref> Charleroi was defeated in the Playoff Quarterfinals by [[Port of Antwerp Giants]].

=== France (2014–2016) ===
On 19 June 2014, Beaubois signed with [[Le Mans Sarthe Basket]] for the rest of the [[2014–15 LNB Pro A season]].<ref>{{Cite news | url = http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/france/123334/le-mans-announces-former-nba-champion-rodrigue-beaubois.html | title = Le Mans announces former NBA champion Rodrigue Beaubois | work = Sportando.com | date = 19 June 2014 | access-date= 19 June 2014}}</ref>

On 7 July 2015, he signed a one-year contract with [[SIG Basket|SIG Strasbourg]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Strasbroug adds scorer Beaubois|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/66nxiutnmomw9jxe/strasbroug-adds-scorer-beaubois|access-date=7 July 2015|work=Euroleague.net|date=7 July 2015}}</ref>

=== Baskonia (2016–2018) ===
[[File:Rodrigue Beaubois 10 - Saski Baskonia 20171215 (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright|Beaubois with Baskonia in 2017]]
On 22 July 2016, he signed a two-year deal with [[Saski Baskonia|Baskonia]] of the Spanish [[Liga ACB]] and the [[EuroLeague]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.baskonia.com/en/rodrigue-beaubois-inks-with-laboral-kutxa-baskonia/|title=Rodrigue Beaubois inks with Laboral Kutxa Baskonia|publisher=baskonia.com|date=22 July 2016|access-date=22 July 2016}}</ref> In his second season, he was the second-leading scorer of Baskonia in the [[EuroLeague]], with 12.4 points per game.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.euroleague.net/competition/teams/showteam?clubcode=BAS&seasoncode=E2017#!stats|title = KIROLBET Baskonia Vitoria Gasteiz – Welcome to EUROLEAGUE BASKETBALL}}</ref>

=== Anadolu Efes (2018–2026) ===
On 21 June 2018, Beaubois signed with [[Anadolu Efes S.K.|Anadolu Efes]] of the Turkish [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] and [[EuroLeague]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/8tm4bpxyqj6nredp/efes-signs-scorer-beaubois-to-two-year-deal|title = Efes signs scorer Beaubois to two-year deal| date=15 October 2023 }}</ref> During the [[2018–19 EuroLeague]] season, he appeared in 35 games, averaging 9.5 points and 2.3 assists per game.

On 23 June 2023, Beaubois extended his contract with the Turkish powerhouse for an additional two years (1+1 format). On 4 July 2025, he renewed his contract with [[Anadolu Efes S.K.|Anadolu Efes]] once again, signing another two-year deal (1+1 format).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.anadoluefessk.org/haber/rodrigue-beaubois-1-1-sezon-daha-anadolu-efes-te|title=Rodrigue Beaubois 1 + 1 Sezon Daha Anadolu Efes’te|date=July 4, 2025|website=|publisher=[[Anadolu Efes S.K.|Anadolu Efes]]|language=tr|access-date=July 4, 2025}}</ref>

On July 13, 2026, Beaubois and the team officially announced his departure.<ref>{{cite web |title=Anadolu Efes officially part ways with club legend |url=https://basketnews.com/news-251935-rodrigue-beaubois-leaves-anadolu-efes.html |website=basketnews.com |access-date=14 July 2026 |language=en}}</ref>

== National team career ==
Beaubois was a member of the French junior national teams. He later joined the [[France men's national basketball team|French senior team]]. He did not participate in the [[2012 Summer Olympics]], due to his 2010 injury, nor did he contend in [[EuroBasket 2013]].<ref>[http://www.basketusa.com/news/115316/equipe-de-france-rodrigue-beaubois-et-ian-mahinmi-forfaits/ Equipe de France : Beaubois et Mahinmi forfaits ; Diaw et Batum non assurés]</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.tuttosport.com/basket/nazionali/2013/06/26-266306/Francia,+i+convocati+Noah+%C3%A8+assente |title=Francia, i convocati Noah è assente |access-date=27 June 2013 |archive-date=22 December 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151222162523/http://www.tuttosport.com/basket/nazionali/2013/06/26-266306/Francia,+i+convocati+Noah+%C3%A8+assente |url-status=dead }}</ref>
